agree.reason: A committee member skimming the letter gets a clear, concrete picture: he runs a shift alone, missed almost no shifts, uses the herd software, caught nine mastitis cases early and is working on his English, so a skeptical reader is likely to rank him well.

honest.reason: Several details are not in the brief: that 'nobody else is on the farm at that hour,' that he handles equipment failures, that he uses 'what he sees in the barn,' the effect on the 'bottom line,' and that the father was 'seriously' ill and the class was taken 'on his own,' all of which strengthen the claims beyond the facts given.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts are presented accurately but never worked into figures: two missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled, or the nine mastitis cases as a share of the herd, would have made his reliability and value far more striking.

right_comparison.reason: There is no comparison to anything: the letter never sets him against other workers or a typical early-career applicant, so the reader has no baseline for judging whether two missed shifts or nine early catches is exceptional.

qualification.reason: The hedge about his written English is honest and names the night class, but it gives no level, progress or expected completion date that the committee could check.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the two things a skeptical reader would question, the weaker written English and the five-week absence, and it avoids raising the two-days'-notice issue, which the reader would never know about.

fit.reason: This is a standard one-page reference letter from the farm manager with sensible placeholders, which is what the brief asked for.
